executiveSummary: GM0274 passes the deterministic ten-preset, six-checkpoint and eight-service numerical contract and has a coherent official 2025 base: Renkum in Gelderland and Veiligheidsregio Gelderland-Midden, 31,490 residents, density 685, 29.7% aged 65-plus, 5,901 one-person households, 54 neighbourhoods in twelve districts, six BAG woonplaatsen, seven BRT settlement labels, Oosterbeek and Wolfheze stations, 96 scheduled-transit stop areas and seven logical A50/A12/N225/N782/N224 links. Rounded neighbourhood populations sum to 31,485, only five below the separately published municipality control (-0.016%). Operational release is nevertheless correction-required. Renkum lies on the Nederrijn and steep Veluwe flank: municipal evidence distinguishes floodplains, brook mouths, shallow groundwater near the Rhine and brooks, deep groundwater elsewhere, push-moraine complexity, sewers and infiltration, while Waterschap Vallei en Veluwe documents a high-water-dependent drainage path from het Broek through the cross-boundary Oranje Nassau's Oord pump. The model instead holds an internal legacy flood-stress amplitude of 1.908693 and severity 0.590524 from T+24 through T+72 without a selected Driel/Nederrijn boundary, defence, floodplain, brook, groundwater, sewer or pump state. Its shared local seed gives eight active unrelated presets the same top hazard-severity order. More critically, the canonical T+24 wildfire radius is 18 km: an official GM0274 boundary vertex is 17.672 km from the ignition while the retained municipal point is 21.087 km away, so the model emits exact zero direct flame without marking it unresolved. Static water structures, routes, rail/transit, capacity/register context and external acute-care records do not establish live topology, passability, capacity, backup or restoration. Exact T+72 persistence, clearance and operational labels lack accountable local actions and verified milestones. Unknown, NoData and static/register values must never become zero hazard, safe, open, available or recovered.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — Gebiedsindelingen 2025, Kerncijfers wijken en buurten, BAG woonplaatsen and BRT settlement context
supports: GM0274 Renkum identity, Gelderland and Gelderland-Midden assignment, generalized municipal boundary and centre 5.7923933, 51.9921589
31,490 residents, density 685, 9,362 people aged 65-plus or 29.7%, 15,037 households and 5,901 one-person households in the municipality control
54 neighbourhood rows in twelve districts; rounded populations total 31,485, households 15,045 and age-65-plus counts 9,370
Six BAG woonplaatsen are Doorwerth, Heelsum, Heveadorp, Oosterbeek, Renkum and Wolfheze; BRT adds Kievitsdel as a deelkern to six woonkern labels
CBS and BRT reuse is CC BY 4.0 and BAG/PDOK is Public Domain Mark 1.0. These are annual administrative/statistical/register facts, not incident-time occupancy or hazard calibration

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Beheerplan Water en Riolering 2022 en verder
supports: Renkum borders the Nederrijn and contains brooks; groundwater is shallow in brook valleys and near the Rhine and varies with river level, while it can be more than seven metres deep elsewhere
Oosterbeek, Heveadorp and Doorwerth lie on the push moraine with complex groundwater behavior
At low river level less than 3% of municipal surface is water, while at high river level more than 13% can be water; floodplains and the mouths of the Renkums and Heelsums brook valleys fill

High river levels can admit river water to sewers, constrain overflow, raise local groundwater and reduce infiltration; local systems, including nominal 40 mm infiltration storage, have separate nuisance, overload and damage objectives

This is authoritative municipal system/planning evidence, not a current hydrograph, complete hydraulic/sewer model, asset operating state or recovery commitment; a standard reuse licence was not stated

evidenceSources.title: E03 — Gemaal Oranje Nassau's Oord and the Renkum Broek high-water drainage path
supports: Het Broek north of Bokkedijk in Renkum remains marshy and historically flooded during high water
The Kortenburgse beek drains toward the pump: at low Rhine level it can discharge freely toward the floodplains, while at high Rhine level the pump removes water from het Broek
Water from the elevated Molenbeek cannot be pumped through this installation and the brook passes under the N225
The installation is therefore a cross-boundary catchment, control and access dependency, not evidence that one containing municipality owns the entire served system
The page supplies system semantics, not live level, pump availability, power/backup, compatible capacity, blockage or restoration; webpage reuse licence was not stated

evidenceSources.title: E04 — Beleidsplan crisisbeheersing Gelderland-Midden 2025–2026 and published regional risk profile context
evidenceSources.edition: 2025–2026 plan, adopted 2024-09-11; references the 2019–2023 risk profile while a 2027–2030 profile is in development
supports: Flooding, nature fire, cybercrime and utility disruption are among the region's highest probability/impact crisis types

The regional profile distinguishes river fluctuation, protected polders and outside-dike land and identifies access, water, vulnerable objects, recreation, safe action and escape as nature-fire response variables
Regional planning supports hazard eligibility and governance but supplies no selected GM0274 event geometry, probability, live resource state, local outcome or T+72 promise
The source's own edition boundary matters: the linked risk profile was prepared in 2019 and the replacement profile was still being developed in 2026; reuse licence was not stated

evidenceSources.title: E05 — Bosbeleidsplan 2018–2028
supports: The municipality states that climate change raises forest-fire risk
Most municipal forest complexes other than Bilderberg are mainly deciduous, which the plan treats as limiting the chance of an uncontrollable fire; risk is heterogeneous rather than absent
Main forest roads are to retain a four-by-four-metre clearance profile for emergency-service access

Forest policy supports combustible-land-cover and response-access eligibility, not current fuel moisture, ignition, perimeter, spread, smoke, people present or suppression capacity; reuse licence was not stated

evidenceSources.title: E06 — Public IMWA/DAMO water assets and nearby Waterinfo Driel observations/forecasts

The realized Oranje Nassau Oord surface-water pump is assigned by point containment to neighbouring GM0289 at 5.7135573, 51.9682456 even though the water board documents its Renkum catchment function; its public capacity is null

No Waterinfo point is assigned inside GM0274. Nearby Driel below and above observations were 614 and 646 cm NAP at 2026-09-02T17:30Z; public Driel forecasts extend only through T+24 in the deployed extract
HWH is CC BY-SA 4.0 with contributor-dependent completeness; Waterinfo is generally CC0, normally updates at ten-minute cadence and is explicitly not mission-critical

identity.summary: Official 2025 identity, regional assignment, centre and generalized boundary agree.
notes: Manifest, generated context and official features identify GM0274 as Renkum in Gelderland and Veiligheidsregio Gelderland-Midden.
The generated centre 5.7923933, 51.9921589 lies inside the official generalized 2025 multipolygon.
The boundary is administrative context, not a hydraulic, fire, smoke, infrastructure or response footprint.

geography.summary: The administrative footprint is coherent but cannot encode Renkum's steep-flank, Nederrijn, brook, groundwater, forest and cross-boundary drainage mechanisms.
notes: The municipality spans elevated push-moraine/forest terrain, steep brook valleys and low floodplain/river-edge areas with materially different water and fire behavior.
Generalized boundaries and centre points do not encode elevation, flow paths, floodplains, sewers, groundwater, defences, pumps, fuels, buildings or road intersections.
The Oranje Nassau Oord record demonstrates that polygon containment is not a service-catchment or ownership graph.

demography.summary: The official municipality control and rounded neighbourhood totals are internally plausible.
notes: The municipality control is 31,490 residents; neighbourhood rows total 31,485, a difference of -5 or -0.016% consistent with source rounding.
Municipality statistics report 9,362 people aged 65-plus, 29.7%, 15,037 households and 5,901 one-person households; summed rounded neighbourhood age-65-plus cells are 9,370 and households 15,045.
Registered residents are not people present during an incident and exclude visitors, workers, pupils, patients and transit/recreation populations.

regionalDetail.summary: Fifty-four neighbourhoods provide useful demographic context but contain explicit gaps and no physical hazard calibration.
notes: All 54 rows contain population and age bands; doctor/supermarket distance is available in 48, household size in 53, cars per household in 33, and several benefit/ownership fields in 36.
District-heating percentage and public charging points are unavailable in all 54 rows; null remains Unknown rather than zero.
Neighbourhood statistics, registered structures, antennas and schools do not establish event exposure, live continuity, backup, access or restoration.

settlements.summary: BAG and BRT place membership is coherent when their distinct semantics are preserved.
notes: Six BAG woonplaatsen are assigned inside the generalized boundary; BRT supplies six woonkernen plus Kievitsdel as one deelkern.
BAG address registration and BRT cartographic labels are complementary and must not be treated as duplicate populations.
Settlements do not provide incident-time occupancy, evacuation zones, service catchments or hazard cells.

The Molenbeek crosses under N225, forest access needs emergency clearance, and A50/N225 routes cross water/topographic systems, but no selected event intersection or operator state is used.

emergencyContext.summary: Authoritative local preparedness, water, forest and regional-risk context exists, but decision-ready incident state and capacity do not.

The public preparedness page supports 72-hour self-preparation but names no active support point or its role, capacity, staffing, accessibility or supplies.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten canonical presets execute at all six checkpoints across all eight services.
notes: Focused audit:model covers T+0, 6, 12, 24, 48 and 72 hours for severe storm, pluvial flood, river flood, coastal flood, heatwave, winter storm, cyberattack, earthquake, wildfire and compound.
The app scenario factory clones the canonical sim-core presets; direct full-network reproductions used the deployed municipality, region and transport data.
Execution coverage does not establish calibration: outputs are deterministic exercise indices, not observations, forecasts, probabilities, casualties or operator commitments.

numericalInvariants.summary: Determinism, finite bounds, allocations, ledgers, burden and layer-invariance contracts pass.
notes: Outputs are finite and non-negative; availability remains in [0,1], zero-event behavior is exact, and cumulative person-hours are monotone.
All service allocations use 54 neighbourhoods and reconcile to the municipality control; service-layer choice does not mutate hazard state.
Arithmetic correctness is necessary but does not validate local forcing, physical allocation, service topology, actions or recovery.

spatialPlausibility.summary: Generic river allocation and municipality-point wildfire logic fail Renkum's physical and official-boundary plausibility tests.
notes: River T+24 and T+72 both report internal legacy flood stress 1.908693 and severity 0.590524 without a selected Nederrijn/Driel, floodplain, brook, groundwater, sewer, defence or pump surface.

Eight nonzero T+24 presets share the same top hazard-severity sequence: Doorwerthse Bossen, Hemelse Berg, Quadenoord, Valkenberg, Heidestein, Keijenberg, Boschhoeve and Klein Zwitserland; the shared seed is independent of mechanism.
The canonical T+24 fire radius is 18 km; official GM0274 geometry reaches 17.672 km from the ignition but its centre is 21.087 km away, producing exact zero flame and no unresolved-fire marker.

serviceDependencies.summary: Water control, utilities, transport, forest access and external care remain static or synthetic rather than causal.
notes: The 101 contained HWH records and cross-boundary Oranje Nassau Oord pump do not form an authority-approved connected operating graph and do not influence the model.
Provider/planning samples, antennas, education sites, roads, rail/transit and hospitals cannot support exact availability, demand, backup, switching, capacity or restoration percentages.
Logical roads transfer only synthetic mobility/supply flow; hazard intersection, direction, closure, emergency accessibility, external care acceptance and water-control state are absent.

causalTrace.summary: Numerical ledgers close, but locally selected events, physical dependencies and accountable actions are absent.
notes: No hydrograph/defence/pump, rain/terrain/groundwater/sewer, fire perimeter/fuel/weather, route/rail, cyber target, utility incident or facility state is selected.

Response lacks owner, trigger, request, decision, resources, dependencies, execution, verification, uncertainty and rollback for warning, evacuation/shelter, water control, fire access, road/rail, external care, utilities and re-entry.
Person-hours reconcile to modelled service deficits, but those deficits are not attributable to locally evidenced events or actions.

recovery72h.summary: Exact hazard clearing, persistent plateaus and operational labels lack local recovery milestones.
notes: River T+24 and T+72 are identical at stress 1.908693, severity 0.590524, 16,877 affected and system pressure 0.520387; burden reaches approximately 1,239,099 person-hours.
Compound T+72 retains flood stress 0.323313, cyber disruption 0.066738, 18,504 affected and approximately 1,296,710 person-hours after rain and wind become zero.

Pluvial and wildfire hazards/affected counts become exact zero by T+72 and the municipality is labelled operational without verified drainage, fire all-clear, access, utility, care, support-point or re-entry milestones.

findings.summary: Official 2025 identity, population and administrative memberships are coherent.
findings.evidence: GM0274 Renkum, Gelderland, Gelderland-Midden, the official centre and generalized boundary agree. Fifty-four rounded neighbourhood populations total 31,485 versus the 31,490 municipality control, a -0.016% difference; six BAG places and seven BRT labels have distinct valid semantics.
findings.action: Retain edition, rounding, suppression and register semantics; never turn controls or place labels into incident-time occupancy.

findings.summary: The complete deterministic numerical and coverage contract passes.
findings.evidence: Ten presets, six checkpoints and eight services execute deterministically with finite bounded values, population/demand/delivery reconciliation, causal ledgers, monotone cumulative burden and layer invariance.
findings.action: Keep GM0274 in regression and add local hydraulic, fire-boundary, cross-boundary water, NoData, access and recovery-action assertions.

findings.summary: A real Nederrijn pathway is represented by unsupported generic forcing and precision.
findings.evidence: At both T+24 and T+72 the model reports internal legacy flood stress 1.908693, severity 0.590524, 16,877 affected and system pressure 0.520387. CORR-017 correctly prevents the legacy scalar being presented as surveyed metres, but no selected Nederrijn/Driel boundary, defence/floodplain, brook mouth, groundwater, sewer/pump state, connected footprint, arrival, recession or uncertainty supports the value.
findings.action: Keep Nederrijn high water eligible but withhold local consequence/recovery until an authority-selected event binds named hydraulic and water-system evidence; unselected cells remain Unknown.

findings.summary: Eight unrelated active hazards reuse exactly one local hazard-severity order.
findings.evidence: At T+24 storm, pluvial, river, heat, winter, cyber, wildfire and compound all rank Doorwerthse Bossen, Hemelse Berg, Quadenoord, Valkenberg, Heidestein, Keijenberg, Boschhoeve and Klein Zwitserland first in the same order. River additionally ranks seed-selected Doorwerthse Bossen first and low-lying Jufferswaard last despite not consuming any terrain or hydraulic surface.
findings.action: Replace the shared rank with mechanism-specific physical/target surfaces and reject complete cross-hazard rank reuse; unsupported neighbourhood cells remain Unknown.

findings.summary: The canonical fire footprint intersects official Renkum geometry but exact direct flame is emitted as zero.
findings.evidence: At T+24 the canonical ignition is 5.75, 52.18 and direct radius 18 km. The retained centre is 21.086866 km away, while an official boundary vertex at 5.7698807, 52.0215408 is 17.672104 km away. The model checks only the centre, yields wildfireIntensity 0 with no unsupported fire dimension, yet emits smoke 0.480814, drought 0.642590, severity 0.173274 and 307 affected.
findings.action: Use polygon intersection and eligible current combustible land cover before local flame allocation; preserve direct flame as Unknown when support intersects but evidence is unresolved, and keep smoke/drought separate.

findings.summary: Precise pluvial stress and clearance omit Renkum's terrain, groundwater, brook, sewer and receiving-water controls.
findings.evidence: Pluvial T+24 reports internal stress 0.312672, severity 0.225819, 2,120 affected and about 115,713 person-hours, then exact zero hazard/affected and operational status at T+72. Municipal evidence describes steep and low areas, variable shallow groundwater, Rhine coupling, brook mouths, sewers and infiltration, but no selected rain, DEM, initial state, network/control state or intervention edition drives the values.
findings.action: Bind an authoritative rain event to terrain, groundwater, brook/surface-water, sewer, pump and infiltration evidence with issue/valid time, resolution, uncertainty, coverage and NoData.

findings.summary: Municipality containment loses the cross-boundary drainage semantics of Oranje Nassau Oord.
findings.evidence: HWH assigns 101 assets inside GM0274, but point-containment assigns realized pump KGM-139 Oranje Nassau Oord to GM0289 with null public capacity. The water board documents that its Kortenburgse-beek path drains Renkum's het Broek under high Rhine levels, while the Molenbeek cannot use the pump. The model consumes neither the catchment nor operating state.
findings.action: Represent authority-approved catchment/control relationships independently from asset-point municipality, including water direction, compatible capacity, power/backup, live state, uncertainty and NoData without exposing sensitive topology.

findings.summary: Forest/water access, A/N-road and rail continuity, and external acute care are not event-valid dependencies.
findings.evidence: Seven logical links, two stations and 96 stops are static context. The water board identifies the Molenbeek/N225 crossing and forest policy requires emergency clearance, while no acute-care site is inside GM0274 and Rijnstate/Gelderse Vallei are external. None can influence response through event intersection, direction, closure, accessibility, referral or destination state.
findings.action: Add authority/operator event-valid, direction-aware routes to affected places, water controls, support points and selected care destinations; never infer passage, travel or capacity from maps, schedules or straight-line distance.

findings.summary: Resident-only allocation does not represent time-varying forest, recreation, school, work, care or transit populations.
findings.evidence: VGGM identifies recreation and vulnerable objects as nature-fire concerns and Renkum addresses residents, visitors and vulnerable people, but every affected count is allocated against the static 31,490 resident control. Schools, stations, forest users, patients and visitors have no time-varying occupancy or uncertainty.
findings.action: Add privacy-safe, time-banded people-present cohorts with authoritative provenance and uncertainty; keep resident-equivalents visibly separate from estimated total people present.

findings.summary: Public water, utility, antenna, education and transport registers do not justify exact service trajectories.
findings.evidence: HWH structures lack an approved connected graph, one NBNL point is planning context, and antenna/education/route records expose no live state, backup, switching, occupancy or restoration. Nonetheless every service receives exact availability, demand, reserve, status and recovery values.
findings.action: Use operator/authority-approved safe aggregate incident and restoration bands with provenance and explicit Unknown; static, planned, null and catalogue no-match values cannot generate operational or recovered state.

findings.summary: Zero direct open-coast stress is narrow scenario scope, not a Renkum water-safety conclusion.
findings.evidence: At T+24 the coastal preset reports zero flood stress and zero affected while retaining wind 15.456802 and small indirect burden. Renkum is inland, but Nederrijn, floodplain, brook, groundwater, sewer and drainage pathways are separate and not tested by that zero.
findings.action: Label direct open-coast impact separately and never generalize zero to river, floodplain, pluvial, groundwater, wind, access or supply safety.

findings.summary: Wind, heat/drought, winter, cyber and remote-earthquake outputs are synthetic and not locally calibrated.
findings.evidence: No selected local weather, heat/vulnerability surface, winter road state, cyber target/incident or earthquake event is bound. At T+24 heat severity is 0.076945, winter 0.617780 and cyber 0.498376; the canonical remote Groningen earthquake has zero local current motion by T+24 but still accumulates indirect service burden.
findings.action: Keep these as explicit exercise assumptions and separate direct from indirect effects; require source, geometry/target, issue/valid time, units, uncertainty, coverage, licence and NoData for operational use.

findings.summary: T+72 plateaus, exact clearance and operational labels lack owner-verified recovery milestones.
findings.evidence: River state is identical at T+24 and T+72 while burden rises to about 1,239,099 person-hours; compound retains stress 0.323313, cyber 0.066738, 18,504 affected and about 1,296,710 person-hours; pluvial and wildfire forcing/affected become exact zero and operational. No water, fire, access, utility, care, support or re-entry action verifies those transitions.
findings.action: Replace exact recovery claims with uncertainty bands and an owner-trigger-decision-resource-execution-verification ledger; keep state Unknown until accountable milestones are met.

residualLimitations: This audit assesses a deterministic exercise model, not a warning, forecast, hydraulic/fire assessment, evacuation order, outage statement, route guarantee, clinical referral or operator commitment.
CBS 2025 neighbourhood values are rounded/suppressed; the -5 population, +8 household and +8 age-65-plus differences are not evidence of missing or extra incident-time people.
Registered residents exclude visitors, workers, pupils, patients, station passengers and people in forest/recreation areas; no complete time-varying occupancy series is consumed.

Generalized municipality/neighbourhood boundaries and centre points are unsuitable for terrain, groundwater, sewer, floodplain, defence, vegetation, building, smoke or route-intersection calculations.
The official water plan documents high-water and local-water mechanisms but is not a live forecast, complete hydraulic/sewer model, asset state or restoration commitment.
The VGGM 2025–2026 plan references an older 2019–2023 risk profile while the 2027–2030 replacement was still under development; neither supplies a selected incident.

Forest policy supports risk/access eligibility only; mainly deciduous composition does not prove no fire and static policy does not provide fuel, moisture, perimeter, spread, occupancy or response state.
HWH's 101 contained records have partial contributor coverage and source-specific/null capacity; register status is not connectivity, compatible throughput, live operation, backup or restoration.
Oranje Nassau Oord illustrates that point containment and administrative ownership differ from catchment/service semantics; its public capacity and live state remain Unknown.
Nearby Driel observations are point- and time-specific; public forecasts ending at T+24 cannot validate municipality-wide or T+72 model state.
NWB, GTFS and ProRail context does not establish live direction, passability, accessibility, emergency throughput, station/rail operation or destination access.
No RIVM acute-care location lies inside GM0274; external registration and straight-line distance do not establish referral, route, occupancy, staffing, diversion, generator endurance or acceptance.
One NBNL postcode sample and RDI/DUO records are planning/register context, not complete topology, current load, incident, backhaul, occupancy, backup or restoration.
The emergency-preparedness page names no current support-point location, activation threshold, staffing, supplies, accessibility or capacity.
No selected local weather, fire, flood, cyber, utility, transport or care incident is bound by publisher, issue/valid time, geometry/target, units, uncertainty, coverage and licence.
Exact synthetic availability can reconcile numerically without validating physical causality, capacity, response decisions or recovery.
Recovery beyond T+72, warning lead, mutual aid, shelter/support capacity, health effects, animal needs and long-term re-entry remain outside locally validated scope.
